prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1153; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received after first notice of loss call. Insured reports a low-speed head-on collision at a parking lot exit. Both vehicles driven at minimal speed. Insured reports no airbag deployment and drivable vehicle on scene. Police report not filed; exchanged information at scene. Assigned field appraisal for both vehicles.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from insured. Insured states other driver reported neck and back discomfort at scene and declined ambulance. Photos of both vehicles uploaded to file showing front bumper contact only, minor crush on the lower fascia. Coverage confirmed under liability and collision on the policy in force at time of loss.

Entry 3: Notice received that claimant is represented by counsel. All further contact to be routed through the attorney's office. Letter of representation placed in file. Requested medical authorization and prior treatment records through counsel. Reserve set pending documentation of the reported back strain.

Entry 4: Medical records received from the claimant's treating provider. Diagnosis listed as lumbar strain with conservative care plan: physical therapy and over-the-counter analgesics. No imaging ordered. Records reviewed against the reported mechanism of injury, which appears consistent with a low-energy impact. Requested itemized bills and wage verification from counsel.

Entry 5: Counsel's demand package received and logged. Under review by claims supervisor. Field appraisal report on the claimant's vehicle indicates repairable damage consistent with photos. Liability assessment in progress. Follow-up scheduled for next review cycle to confirm treatment status and outstanding bills.
